title: Broken Well
tagline: The well never holds its shape. Clear it, or outlast the flood.
teaser: The owner's earlier port of the 1992 Berkeley falling-blocks game, where the well keeps changing shape: a canyon, a split pillar, an hourglass neck, a standing pillar. Hold back a rising flood, and rise from Hand Digger to Master of the Broken Well through twelve shifts and a Daily Shift.

manPage.synopsis: blocks-classic — a falling-blocks shift in a well the quarry keeps reshaping; clear the line target or outlast the rising rubble.
manPage.description: The owner's earlier fancy-web port of the BSD falling-blocks original: seven tetrominoes, a next-piece preview, a ghost piece, a seven-bag randomizer, wall kicks and lock delay, all playing inside a well whose shape changes shift to shift — a canyon, a split pillar, an hourglass neck, a donut of standing rock, a staircase floor, a narrow tower, a wide cut — with an optional starting rubble stack and a flood mode where rubble rises from below. Around it, a quarry foreman's career of twelve shifts with ranks, a briefing of three contracts and a seal for each, a written logbook of every shift, a Free Dig mode and a Daily Shift. A second interpretation beside the collection's own Sinkers.

howToPlay: Move with ← / → (or A / D), rotate with ↑ / W / X clockwise and Z counter-clockwise.
↓ / S soft-drops; Space hard-drops onto the ghost outline below the falling piece.
Clear a shift's line target in the Long Dig, or hold the well through its rubble rows in the Rising Flood.
